title: Variance with a Hole in the Data
scenario: It is 6:25 AM. The clean table has three hubs, but the forecast file only covers two of them - WAUE was added to the desk last month and the forecast model does not know it yet. Compute what can be computed, and exclude what cannot, explicitly.
input:
hub, actual, forecast, priorDay
ERCOT, 204, 188, 176
SPP, 98.5, 100, 97
WAUE, 63, (no forecast), 59

Desk rule: a variance row requires BOTH references. A hub missing a reference is excluded from the variance summary and reported through the exception process - do not fabricate a forecast for WAUE, and do not include a partial row.
instructions: For each fully-referenced hub, compute vsForecast = actual - forecast and vsPriorDay = actual - priorDay.
Decimals are allowed and negatives are allowed.
WAUE has no forecast: exclude it entirely per the desk rule.
Return a JSON array with one object per computable hub, then validate.
copilotPrompt: Compute vsForecast = actual - forecast and vsPriorDay = actual - priorDay for each hub that has BOTH references. ERCOT: 204/188/176. SPP: 98.5/100/97. WAUE has no forecast, so exclude it entirely - do not fabricate a value. Return a JSON array of { hub, vsForecast, vsPriorDay }.
successMessage: Variance computed where it could be, excluded where it could not - and the difference is visible instead of invented.

intro.heading: Before you build: compute honestly or not at all

sections.title: Partial data is the default
sections.body: New hubs, late files, renamed keys - real reference data has holes. The mature move is not heroics; it is a rule: compute the rows you can defend, exclude the ones you cannot, and say so.

sections.title: Why exclusion beats invention
sections.body: Any number you invent for WAUE's vsForecast will be consumed downstream as if it were real. An absent row is a visible gap the workflow can route around; a fabricated value is an invisible error it cannot.

sections.title: Decimals carry signal
sections.body: SPP came in at 98.5 against a forecast of 100 - a delta of -1.5. Rounding it away to 'about zero' would erase the direction. Keep the precision the sources gave you.

fieldGuide.meaning: One row per hub with complete references.
fieldGuide.hint: Two hubs qualify. One does not - why?
Negatives and decimals are part of the signal.

takeaway.heading: Variance with a visible gap
points: You computed defensible deltas for the hubs with complete references, keeping decimal precision.
You excluded WAUE instead of fabricating its forecast - the gap stays visible instead of becoming an invisible error.
The exclusion rule came from governance (both references required), not from your mood at 6:25 AM.
Risk Evaluation on this tier will still classify WAUE using the day-over-day data that DOES exist - different steps, different requirements.
The workflow can now produce partial-but-honest derived data when its references have holes.
